answer: Sequential provenance chain. Each new agent identity must inherit a signed history from a prior agent, and the first link in any chain is an opal certificate issued only after completing a unique, verifiable voyage (a logged physical or computational journey that cannot be cloned). The cedar registry anchors each chain's origin and enforces that no root certificate seeds more than one descendant per epoch. An attacker must physically repeat each voyage to mint a new identity, paying the full time and travel cost per sybil, which scales linearly and cannot be amortized across copies.
